outcome: Codify the QPF trust-substrate thesis as a canonical architecture specification: QPF is verification infrastructure independent of model, agent, identity, execution, authorization, and settlement layers. Documentation only; no code or protocol semantics changes.
forbiddenActions: minting, staking, liquidity, or bridge enablement
definitionOfDone: The specification clearly establishes QPF as verification infrastructure rather than a model provider.
Model, agent, identity, verification, execution, authorization, and settlement boundaries are explicit.
Cryptographic validity is explicitly distinguished from semantic correctness and real-world truth.
pass/fail/partial/unavailable semantics are preserved; VALID/INVALID/INCOMPLETE/CONFLICT phrasing is attributed to its governing governance-receipt context and not presented as verifier output codes.
Provider independence is defined as a testable architectural property, not a claimed achievement.
Existing QPF adversarial-verification work is referenced without overstating conclusions.
No live economic or privileged execution capability is enabled.
Existing canonical documents are not contradicted.
